gaps: Southeast Asian coverage is thinner than ideal from the allowed-domain editorial sources, especially for Neukölln/Wedding/Friedrichshain regional specialists with full address extraction.
Turkish/Middle Eastern/Caucasus section has strong Turkish grill and Georgian options, but Persian/Armenian/Azerbaijani/Yemeni specialist coverage remains limited in the fetched material.
Mediterranean/European section skews Austrian/modern European; stronger Italian, Spanish, Greek, or Balkan candidates in the preferred neighborhoods would improve balance.
Several promising candidates lack exact street numbers because the accessible source snippets were partial or blocked; these need confirmation in the separate Places step before final briefing use.
Mitte surfaced more than desired because allowed editorial sources disproportionately cover central openings and Michelin picks.
search_notes: One combined editorial-source pass was run under the strict allowed-domain constraint. Priority was given to Berlin Food Stories, tipBerlin, Cee Cee, and Michelin because they provided the most usable name/address/cuisine detail without resorting to Google Maps. Some tipBerlin pages returned fetch limitations, so a few candidates are included with partial address data only and should be verified in the later Places step. I avoided unsupported hype-only openings and tried to bias toward affordable specialists, grills, noodle houses, and regionally specific kitchens. Fine dining was kept to two credible Michelin-backed candidates only.
